findings.title: Cache key uses Python hash(), which is not stable across processes
findings.body: The cache key is built with `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`. Python's built-in `hash()` for tuples of ints is salted per process (PYTHONHASHSEED), so the same project-id set produces different keys in different workers/processes. Consequence: cache entries written by one worker can never be read by another (cache hit rate collapses, defeating the stated performance goal), and worse, `invalidate_upsampling_cache` (line 73) computes the key in whichever process handles the config change, so it will almost never delete the keys other workers are reading — stale eligibility can persist well beyond 60s. Use a deterministic encoding such as a sorted, joined string of project ids.

findings.title: Upsampling eligibility is checked against the outer dataset, not the scoped dataset actually queried
findings.body: In `_get_event_stats`, `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects(snuba_params, organization, dataset, request)` uses the closed-over `dataset` variable, but the query is executed against `scoped_dataset`. In the dashboard-widget split path (`get_event_stats_factory`), `_get_event_stats` is invoked with `split_dataset` = `discover` or `metrics_enhanced_performance` while the outer `dataset` may be different, so the decision to substitute `upsampled_count()` is made against the wrong dataset. This can either apply a `sample_weight`-based aggregation to a dataset that has no such column (query error) or skip it for an errors-only split query where it should apply. Pass `scoped_dataset` instead.

findings.title: Only exact 'count()' is transformed, producing inconsistent mixed-scaled results
findings.body: `transform_query_columns_for_error_upsampling` rewrites only the literal string `count()` and leaves every other aggregation untouched. A request like `yAxis=count(),count_unique(user),p95(transaction.duration)` on an allowlisted errors query will return an upsampled (scaled) count alongside unsampled-based unique/percentile values in the same response, giving internally inconsistent data (e.g. unique users can exceed total count). Aliased forms such as `count() as total` are also missed. Either transform the other supported aggregations or restrict the rewrite to requests whose entire column list can be upsampled.

findings.title: Error-focus check inspects the raw request query, not the effective query
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` reads `request.GET['query']`, but the actual query executed by `_get_event_stats` can be a rewritten one (e.g. the dashboard split path builds `f"({query}) AND !event.type:transaction"`, and other callers pass scoped queries). A discover query that filters errors via the rewritten query but whose original request query lacks `event.type:error` will silently skip upsampling, while an equivalent query phrased differently gets it. The decision should be derived from the query string actually being executed, not the raw request parameter.

findings.title: No caller for invalidate_upsampling_cache and no cache-invalidation on option change
findings.body: `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is defined but never invoked anywhere in this PR, and nothing hooks it to changes of the `issues.client_error_sampling.project_allowlist` option. Combined with the 60s cache and the broken (hash-based) key, removing a project from the allowlist may not take effect for an unbounded time. Either wire invalidation into the option-update path or drop the cache.

findings.title: Snuba endpoint upsampling tests are order-dependent due to shared cache state
findings.body: `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` writes its result to the shared cache under a key derived from organization id and project ids. The four tests in `OrganizationEventsStatsErrorUpsamplingTest` use the same org/projects but different mocked allowlists, and nothing clears the cache between them. `test_error_upsampling_with_allowlisted_projects` caches `True`, so the later `test_error_upsampling_with_partial_allowlist` / `..._with_no_allowlisted_projects` can read the stale cached value and fail (or pass only due to run order). The tests must flush the cache in setUp, and the new unit tests never exercise `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` (including its cache branch) at all.

findings.title: Accidental nested git repository / submodule entry committed
findings.body: The PR adds a `sentry-repo` file containing 'Subproject commit ...', which indicates a nested git checkout was committed to the repository root. This pollutes the repo and should be removed (and gitignored) before merge.

findings.title: Comments claim caching/consistency behavior the code does not provide
findings.body: The comments in `_get_event_stats` say the eligibility check is 'cached' and ensures 'consistent behavior across query execution', and `upsampling_enabled = should_upsample` is a pointless alias. The helper's own docstring also claims the allowlist is read 'fresh each time', directly contradicting the 60-second cache in the same function. These misleading comments should be corrected or removed since they describe guarantees (freshness, consistency) the implementation explicitly does not have.
